lines.speaker: narrator
lines.subtitle: Torvald's frontier, a week before the snows.|A wall older than any of the four.
lines.text: Torvald's frontier, a week before the snows. A wall older than any of the four.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: The Wall of a Hundred Winters. While it stands,|this war never has to stop for weather.
lines.text: The Wall of a Hundred Winters. While it stands, this war never has to stop for weather.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: So we knock it down. I brought fire.|You brought... a tree?
lines.text: So we knock it down. I brought fire. You brought... a tree?

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: Several. They're very patient,|and they hit like a landslide.
lines.text: Several. They're very patient, and they hit like a landslide.

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: Under the ice by the west gate, something old|is sleeping. Wake it, and it will owe you.
lines.text: Under the ice by the west gate, something old is sleeping. Wake it, and it will owe you.

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: Good morning, grandfather.|There's a wall that needs leaning on.
lines.text: Good morning, grandfather. There's a wall that needs leaning on.

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: Ysolde. I warned you about the cold.|Turn back while the passes are open.
lines.text: Ysolde. I warned you about the cold. Turn back while the passes are open.

lines.speaker: shade
lines.subtitle: The Bishop sends his tithe, Lord Torvald.|He asks for nothing in return. Yet.
lines.text: The Bishop sends his tithe, Lord Torvald. He asks for nothing in return. Yet.

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: Nothing is what Malrik|always asks for. At first.
lines.text: Nothing is what Malrik always asks for. At first.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: The Heartwood stands tall again.|Let the elders come.
lines.text: The Heartwood stands tall again. Let the elders come.

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: Now that is a tree with opinions.
lines.text: Now that is a tree with opinions.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: I'm taking the east gate. Don't wait for me.|I definitely won't wait for you.
lines.text: I'm taking the east gate. Don't wait for me. I definitely won't wait for you.

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: I built this wall so nobody would ever|have to choose. You are making me choose.
lines.text: I built this wall so nobody would ever have to choose. You are making me choose.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: No, Torvald. Malrik made you choose.|I'm only here to hear the answer.
lines.text: No, Torvald. Malrik made you choose. I'm only here to hear the answer.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: A gate's down! Your trees punch harder than|my fire, Ysolde. I hate it. Keep going.
lines.text: A gate's down! Your trees punch harder than my fire, Ysolde. I hate it. Keep going.

lines.speaker: aldra
lines.subtitle: Wake, old guards. Somebody is knocking.
lines.text: Wake, old guards. Somebody is knocking.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: Colossi. Tall, slow, and stubborn. So are we.
lines.text: Colossi. Tall, slow, and stubborn. So are we.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: Shadow at my hearths, Ysolde!|If your trees can walk, now's the time.
lines.text: Shadow at my hearths, Ysolde! If your trees can walk, now's the time.

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: One mountain fewer. Mountains are overrated.
lines.text: One mountain fewer. Mountains are overrated.

lines.speaker: shade
lines.subtitle: The second tithe, Lord Torvald.|The Bishop says: no more excuses.
lines.text: The second tithe, Lord Torvald. The Bishop says: no more excuses.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.subtitle: The wardens are rubble. The Winterheart|stands alone, and it is cracking.
lines.text: The wardens are rubble. The Winterheart stands alone, and it is cracking.

lines.speaker: aldra
lines.subtitle: You thawed his wood, Ysolde.|You will not thaw his wall.
lines.text: You thawed his wood, Ysolde. You will not thaw his wall.

lines.speaker: aldra
lines.subtitle: You broke my glass once,|Ysolde. Once was enough.
lines.text: You broke my glass once, Ysolde. Once was enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.subtitle: A hundred winters, broken in one|afternoon. The Wall begins to weep.
lines.text: A hundred winters, broken in one afternoon. The Wall begins to weep.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: Look at it melt! Fire always wins in the end.
lines.text: Look at it melt! Fire always wins in the end.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: That was the tree, Vessa.
lines.text: That was the tree, Vessa.

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: The glass spire. Aldra will|be waiting. She always is.
lines.text: The glass spire. Aldra will be waiting. She always is.

lines.speaker: vessa
lines.subtitle: Both halls! Torvald's soldiers will|have to train in the snow. Good.
lines.text: Both halls! Torvald's soldiers will have to train in the snow. Good.

lines.speaker: aldra
lines.subtitle: One strike, Torvald, and the green|war is over. Let me finish it.
lines.text: One strike, Torvald, and the green war is over. Let me finish it.

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: Enough, Aldra.
lines.text: Enough, Aldra.

lines.speaker: aldra
lines.subtitle: She broke your wall!
lines.text: She broke your wall!

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: It was only ever ice. Let her up.
lines.text: It was only ever ice. Let her up.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: Why?
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: torvald
lines.subtitle: Because a hundred winters is long enough.|Go home, Ysolde. Spring will keep.
lines.text: Because a hundred winters is long enough. Go home, Ysolde. Spring will keep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.subtitle: That night the first blizzard closed the passes.|Both sides sat down to wait for spring.
lines.text: That night the first blizzard closed the passes. Both sides sat down to wait for spring.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.subtitle: Plant me... somewhere warm...
lines.text: Plant me... somewhere warm...

lines.speaker: maelis
lines.subtitle: The Heartwood's fallen. Winter wins this one.
lines.text: The Heartwood's fallen. Winter wins this one.
